transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess the main thing that made me come in is my appetite’s been really off the last few weeks. Like, I work security—surveillance kind of stuff—and usually after a shift I know exactly what I want to eat, even if it’s just something simple I like. But lately I’ll get food in front of me and it just kind of sits there. I’ll take a few bites because I know I should eat, but I’m basically forcing it down.

It’s not like I’m trying to diet or anything. Food just doesn’t sound good, even stuff I normally look forward to. After a shift I used to be pretty hungry, and now it’s more like I stare at it and think, “I should probably eat this,” but I don’t really want it. That’s what’s been worrying me enough to come in.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood or interest in activities lately?

Yeah… I have. It’s kind of hard to explain because it’s not like I’m walking around crying all day or anything like that. It’s more like this heavy, flat feeling is just there most days, like I’m carrying it around with me.

Even when I’m at home with my family, I’ll be in the room, sitting there, hearing people talk or whatever’s going on, and I don’t feel fully there. Same thing at work, like in the break room—guys might be joking around or talking, and I’m physically sitting there, but inside I just feel sort of distant. Like everything is muted, I guess.

I still go through the motions, but there’s this weight to everything that wasn’t there before. It makes it harder to really connect with what’s happening around me.
Have you noticed feeling more tired or lacking energy lately, even if you’re not doing anything physically demanding?

I don’t know that I’d say that exactly. I mean, I get tired like anyone does, especially depending on the shift, but I haven’t really noticed a big change where I’m just exhausted all the time or anything.

It’s more like… I feel off, but I wouldn’t point to energy as the main thing. I can still get through what I need to do. If I’m sitting around, I don’t think I feel physically worn out for no reason. I guess I’m not totally sure how to separate tired from just feeling kind of weighed down, but I haven’t been thinking, like, “Why am I so tired?” all day.
Have you found that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, even activities or hobbies that you normally like?

Yeah… yeah, I have. That’s actually been one of the weirder parts of it, because it’s not like anything changed with those things themselves. I used to really look forward to my morning runs. Not even in a hardcore fitness way, just… it was part of my routine, and it helped me feel like I was starting the day right. Lately I’ll set my stuff out or think, “I should go,” and then I just don’t. It feels like this whole production I can’t make myself care about.

Same with guitar. I used to pick it up without thinking, even if it was just messing around for ten minutes. Now it’s sitting there and I look at it like it’s another task on a list. Cooking dinner too—I used to actually enjoy that, planning something simple, making it for the house, that kind of thing. But now even that feels like a chore. I keep skipping it or doing the bare minimum because I just don’t feel the same pull toward it.

It’s not that I hate those things now. It’s more like the enjoyment got drained out of them somehow, and I can’t really get myself to care the way I normally would.
Would you say that you feel down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, even if it's not severe?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, “depressed” is a word I don’t always know how to use, because I’m still getting up and going to work and doing the normal stuff, so part of me wants to say, “Well, it’s not that bad.” But most days, yeah, there’s this heavy, flat feeling that’s kind of just with me.

It’s there when I’m home with my family, even if nothing’s wrong in that moment. I’ll be sitting there and everyone’s around, and I know I should feel more present or more connected, but I just feel like I’m not really there. Same thing at work, like if I’m in the break room and people are talking or joking around, I can hear it all, but it’s like I’m watching it from a step back or something.

So yeah, most of the day, most days, it’s not necessarily severe like I can’t function, but it’s there. Like a low ceiling over everything.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to think clearly, concentrate, or make decisions lately?

Yeah… that one I have noticed, actually. It’s not like I’m confused about where I am or anything like that, but I’m definitely not as sharp as I usually am.

At work, when I’m watching the CCTV feeds, my mind kind of drifts. I’ll realize I’ve been looking at the screens but not really taking in what I’m seeing, if that makes sense. Like my eyes are on it, but my brain is somewhere else. And then with incident reports, I keep having to reread what I wrote or reread the same section because it doesn’t stick the first time. I’ll read a sentence and then immediately think, “Wait, what did that say?” and go back over it again.

That’s not really normal for me. I mean, that job is a lot of paying attention to small details, and I’ve always been pretty good about that. Lately I’ve made a couple mistakes I wouldn’t usually make, just little things, but still. It bothers me because it’s the kind of stuff I normally catch. So yeah, concentration and thinking clearly have been harder than usual.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately, like trouble falling asleep, waking up a lot during the night, or sleeping much more than usual?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that one, honestly. I don’t think I’ve noticed some big, obvious change like… I don’t know, being up all night every night or suddenly sleeping half the day. It hasn’t stood out to me the way some of the other stuff has.

I mean, I have nights where I’m not sleeping great, but I feel like everybody has those, and I haven’t really been keeping track of it closely. Sometimes I’ll lie there longer than I’d like, but I don’t know if that’s new or just me paying more attention because I’m already feeling off. And I don’t think I’ve been waking up constantly or anything dramatic like that.

So… maybe a little unsettled here and there, but I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed a clear pattern or a major change in my sleep.
Have you been sleeping more or less than usual, or do you feel unrested even after a full night's sleep?

I don’t really know that I can say one way or the other. Like, I haven’t been looking at the clock and thinking, “Oh, I’m sleeping way less,” or “I’m sleeping way more,” if that makes sense.

I do have mornings where I don’t feel especially refreshed, but I’m not sure if that’s sleep exactly or just… normal life, stress, being tired from work, that kind of thing. I don’t want to overstate it and say there’s been some clear pattern, because I honestly haven’t noticed one. It’s not like I’m sleeping all day, and it’s not like I’m barely sleeping at all.

So I guess my answer is: maybe it hasn’t felt perfect, but I haven’t noticed a major change in the amount I’m sleeping or a consistent thing where a full night still leaves me feeling wiped out.
Have you noticed any days where you feel like you don’t have the energy to even get through simple tasks, or where everything feels like it takes extra effort?

I don’t think so, not in a clear way. I mean, I have days where I drag a little, sure, especially if work’s been boring or long, but I wouldn’t say I’ve had that thing where brushing my teeth or making food or taking a shower feels impossible or anything like that.

Simple tasks are still getting done. Maybe I’m slower with some things because my head’s not fully in it, but energy-wise… I don’t know, I haven’t really noticed a big drop. It’s not like I’m stuck on the couch all day unable to move. I still get up, go to work, handle the basic stuff.

So I guess I’d say everything might feel a little more effortful sometimes, but not to the point where I’d call it a major problem or something I’ve really been tracking.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, even things you previously looked forward to doing?

Yeah… that one I think I can answer more clearly. I have noticed that, actually.

It’s not like I never do anything at all, but the stuff I used to kind of look forward to just feels… flat now, or like another thing on the list. I used to really like going for a run in the morning. Not in some intense athlete way, but it was something that made me feel like I’d started the day right. Lately I keep skipping it, and when I think about going, it just feels like a chore instead of something I want to do.

Same with playing guitar. I used to pick it up without even thinking about it, just mess around for a while after work. Now it’ll sit there and I’ll look at it and think, “I should play,” but I don’t really feel anything about it, so I don’t.

And cooking dinner too. I used to enjoy making something decent, even simple stuff, but lately it feels like too much trouble and like I can’t get myself to care about it. It’s weird, because these are things I know I used to enjoy, but right now they just don’t have the same pull.
Have you lost or gained a significant amount of weight recently, without trying to diet or change your eating habits?

I haven’t been trying to lose weight or anything, no. I don’t really know the exact number, because I’m not weighing myself every day, but the appetite thing has definitely been off.

Honestly, that’s part of why I came in. For the last few weeks, I’ve barely felt hungry. Like after a shift, normally I’d be pretty ready to eat, and there are certain things I usually like or at least look forward to, but lately I’ll make something or pick something up and it just kind of sits there. I’ll take a few bites because I know I should eat, not because I actually want it.

It’s not like I made some big diet change or decided to eat healthier. It’s more that food just doesn’t sound good, even when it should. Sometimes I’ll look at a meal and feel like I have to force it down a little, which is not really normal for me.
Have you felt down or had a low mood most of the day, nearly every day, for at least the past two years?

Two years? I don’t know if I’d say it that way. I mean, I haven’t been keeping track like that, and “nearly every day for two years” sounds very specific.

But most days lately, yeah, I do feel low. It’s like I’m carrying this heavy, flat feeling around with me. Not always crying or anything dramatic like that, just… dulled out, I guess. Even when I’m home with my family, or sitting in the break room at work, I’ll be physically there, but I don’t really feel present. Like I’m watching myself get through the day instead of actually being in it.

Some days it lifts a little, or I can distract myself for a while, but a lot of the time there’s this low mood just sitting there in the background. I’m not sure how long exactly, but it’s been noticeable.
Would you say that most days, for at least the past two years, you’ve felt down or low, even if it wasn’t every single day?

Most days, yes… but I don’t know that I can honestly say it’s been two full years. That part is hard for me to answer exactly.

What I can say is that most days lately I feel like I’m carrying this heavy, flat feeling around with me. It’s not always dramatic or obvious from the outside. I can still go through the motions, talk to people, be at home with my family, sit in the break room at work, whatever—but a lot of the time I feel like I’m not really there. Like I’m present physically, but mentally I’m kind of distant or dulled out.

So if you’re asking whether feeling low has become more of a regular thing than just an occasional bad day, then yeah, it has. I just don’t want to overstate it and say “two years” if I’m not sure.

I haven’t been trying to lose weight or anything, no. I don’t really know the exact number, because I’m not weighing myself every day, but the appetite thing has definitely been off.

Honestly, that’s part of why I came in. For the last few weeks, I’ve barely felt hungry. Like after a shift, normally I’d be pretty ready to eat, and there are certain things I usually like or at least look forward to, but lately I’ll make something or pick something up and it just kind of sits there. I’ll take a few bites because I know I should eat, not because I actually want it.

It’s not like I made some big diet change or decided to eat healthier. It’s more that food just doesn’t sound good, even when it should. Sometimes I’ll look at a meal and feel like I have to force it down a little, which is not really normal for me.

doctor.question: Have you felt down or had a low mood most of the day, nearly every day, for at least the past two years?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: Most days I feel like I’m carrying this heavy, flat feeling around, like even when I’m home with my family or sitting in the break room, I’m just not really there.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question is most directly asking about persistent low or depressed mood, even though it includes a two-year duration qualifier.

patient.answer:
Two years? I don’t know if I’d say it that way. I mean, I haven’t been keeping track like that, and “nearly every day for two years” sounds very specific.

But most days lately, yeah, I do feel low. It’s like I’m carrying this heavy, flat feeling around with me. Not always crying or anything dramatic like that, just… dulled out, I guess. Even when I’m home with my family, or sitting in the break room at work, I’ll be physically there, but I don’t really feel present. Like I’m watching myself get through the day instead of actually being in it.

Some days it lifts a little, or I can distract myself for a while, but a lot of the time there’s this low mood just sitting there in the background. I’m not sure how long exactly, but it’s been noticeable.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a depressed mood for at least two years, which would support a diagnosis of persistent depressive disorder (F34.1) rather than major depressive disorder (F32.1 or F33.1).
doctor.question: Would you say that most days, for at least the past two years, you’ve felt down or low, even if it wasn’t every single day?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: Most days I feel like I’m carrying this heavy, flat feeling around, like even when I’m home with my family or sitting in the break room, I’m just not really there.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about feeling down or low most days over time, which directly corresponds to depressed mood.

patient.answer:
Most days, yes… but I don’t know that I can honestly say it’s been two full years. That part is hard for me to answer exactly.

What I can say is that most days lately I feel like I’m carrying this heavy, flat feeling around with me. It’s not always dramatic or obvious from the outside. I can still go through the motions, talk to people, be at home with my family, sit in the break room at work, whatever—but a lot of the time I feel like I’m not really there. Like I’m present physically, but mentally I’m kind of distant or dulled out.

So if you’re asking whether feeling low has become more of a regular thing than just an occasional bad day, then yeah, it has. I just don’t want to overstate it and say “two years” if I’m not sure.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a persistent low mood, diminished interest/pleasure in activities, reduced appetite, and impaired concentration, occurring most days for a duration that appears to exceed two years. These symptoms are consistent with a diagnosis of moderate recurrent depressive disorder, particularly given the chronic course and absence of a clear two-week limit that would favor a diagnosis of major depressive disorder. The chronicity and symptom pattern differentiate F33.1 from F32.1 (moderate major depressive disorder), which is time-limited.
